reports.title: Dell Technologies Delivers Third Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results

guidance.heading: Guidance Summary
section: (in billions, except percentages and per share amounts)

desk.headline: Revenue more than doubled to $54.9bn and adjusted EPS of $9.45, well above estimates; FY27 outlook raised to $202bn
results: Revenue rose 103% to a record $54.9bn, far above the $49.3bn estimate; adjusted EPS of $9.45 beat the $6.55 estimate.
Infrastructure drove it: ISG revenue nearly tripled to $42.0bn, with AI servers at $22.0bn and traditional servers and networking at $15.0bn.
ISG operating income quadrupled to $7.1bn, while the PC business grew 3% and its operating income fell 6% to $704m.
Non-GAAP operating costs fell to 7% of revenue from 11.8%, lifting the non-GAAP operating margin to 14.2% from 9.3%.
Operating cash flow was $4.5bn; Dell returned $4.9bn through buybacks and dividends and added $25bn to its buyback authorisation.

guidance.summary: Dell raised its FY27 outlook to $202bn of revenue (up 78%) and adjusted EPS of $29.68, and expects AI server sales of $78bn. For Q4 it guides to $56.3bn of revenue and adjusted EPS of $8.40.

points: COO Jeff Clarke said AI demand is speeding up and spreading worldwide, with $60.2bn of AI orders booked in the quarter.
The AI backlog reached a record $132.3bn; Clarke said no customer has pushed orders back and called it "very firm".
Each AI order is checked for the buyer's access to funding, power and land, and Dell says it is choosy with newer cloud providers.
Management expects the gap between AI demand and supply to widen next year.
Some customers are delaying PC upgrades to fund servers, and Dell is shifting chips from PCs to server builds.
call.source: Call coverage: Yahoo Finance, 24 Nov 2026; Stocktwits, 24 Nov 2026
